name: Vigilante Masked Grappler
body:
The life of a vigilante is often lived with attention all around them, reveling in the adulation of crowds as they stand proud above fallen foes. There are those who employ more close range tactics, fighting with their bare hands as they crush their foes with expert maneuvers.

Weapon and Armor Proficiencies

Masked grapplers are not proficient with martial weapons or medium armor. This alters A vigilante’s weapon and armor proficiencies.

Grappling Genius (Ex)

At 1st level, a masked grappler gains the Improved Unarmed Strike and Improved Grapple feat, using their masked grappler level in place of their base attack bonus when calculating their Combat Maneuver Bonus when making grapple combat maneuvers. Base attack bonuses granted from other classes are unaffected and are added normally. Whenever a masked grappler deals damage with a grapple check (including submissions and techniques), they deal additional damage equal to 1/2 their masked grappler level (minimum 1). At 6th level, the masked grappler gains the Greater Grapple feat. This ability replaces vigilante specialization.

Grappling Talents (Ex)

At 2nd level, a masked grappler can select two new types of vigilante talents; submissions and techniques. The masked grappler can use one of these techniques whenever they successfully maintain a grapple or pin. Submissions and techniques deal damage as if the masked grappler chose to deal damage with their grapple, and after using a technique, the grapple is ended for both the masked wrestler and their foe. Using a technique or submission ends the masked grappler’s turn. If a masked grappler continues to use a submission which causes their foe to suffer a penalty, that penalty is increased by 1 for each round the submission is maintained as well as resetting the duration of the penalty.

A masked grappler using a submission talent must use the grapple check needed to maintain a grapple to continue the submission or end the submission. Each round the masked grappler maintains a submission, their opponent suffers a -1 penalty against saving throws for that submission. The masked grappler uses their Constitution modifier to determine the saving throws of their vigilante techniques in place of their Charisma modifier, and they must select either a submission or technique for their first vigilante talent.

A masked grappler can select from any of the following vigilante talents, in addition to general vigilante talents.

Anklelock (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler twists the ankle of a foe as hard as they can, attempting to snap their foe’s ankle. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or have their base land speed be reduced by 10 feet (to a minimum of 0 feet) and take a -3 penalty to reflex saves for 1 minute. At 8th level this penalty increases to 15 ft. and -4. This talent does not work on foes without legs.

Armbar (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler manages to wrench a foe’s arm or other limb, attempting to snap it. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take a -1 penalty on all attacks for 1 minute. At 6th level, this penalty increases to -2. At 12th level this penalty increases to -3. This talent does not work on foes without limbs.

Bearhug (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler grabs a foe and squeezes the life from out of them. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or be fatigued for 1 minute. At 10th level, the foe is instead exhausted.

Bodyslam (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler is capable of lifting creatures up to one size larger than themselves or smaller into the air and dropping them onto their back, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. Both you and your foe fall prone after this technique. At 10th level, this talent deals additional damage equal to twice the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier, and they no longer fall prone after using it. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.

Chokehold (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler wraps their limbs around the foe’s airway, cutting off their breathing. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or have the air expelled from their lungs, and must make saves against drowning as long as the submission is maintained. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent, and does not work on foes without heads or foes that do not need to breathe.

Frog Splash (Ex)

Whenever a masked grappler is standing on a solid surface 5 ft. or higher than a prone foe, they can make an Acrobatics check to jump into the foe’s square, making an unarmed strike against them which deals two times as much damage. If the attack is successful, the masked grappler can make a grapple check as a swift action to pin them. For every 10 ft. that the masked grappler falls to make this attack, they deal an additional +1d6 damage, and the masked grappler only takes falling damage if they miss with this attack. At 6th level and every 6 levels afterwards, the masked grappler can treat themselves as 10 ft. higher for the purposes of how much damage this talent deals.

Full Nelson (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler pins the arms of their foe behind them, applying pressure to their arms. The foe must make a Reflex saving throw or be flat?footed for the duration of this submission, providing cover to the masked grappler. At 6th level, all attacks against a foe in this submission gain +2 precision damage. This damage increases to +4 at 12th level and +6 at 18th level, and this submission does not work on foes without arms.

Hard Whip (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler whips their foe forward, forcing them 30 feet in a direction of their choice. This movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity, and if the foe’s movement is stopped by a solid barrier such as a wall, they take 1d6 damage and are bounced in the opposite direction for the remaining distance. Foes that enter a square threatened by the masked grappler after being bounced provoke an attack of opportunity from them, which must be made with an unarmed strike. This movement is ended if the foe would be bounced twice. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.

Hurricanrana (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler jumps onto their foe and throws them forward with their legs, disorientating them. The foe must make a Reflex saving throw or be flat-footed for 1 round. At 8th level, the foe is flat-footed for 2 rounds. At 16th level, the foe is flat-footed for 3 rounds.

Joint Lock (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler knows how to break bones with their submissions. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take 1d3 Dexterity damage. At 12th level, this damage increases to 1d4 Dexterity damage. At 16th level, this damage increases to 1d6 Dexterity damage. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.

Lightweight Grappler (Ex)

A masked grappler uses their Dexterity modifier in place of their Strength modifier for grapple checks and in place of their Constitution modifier when determining the damage of techniques and submissions.

Kip Up (Ex)

Whenever a masked grappler is prone, they can stand as a swift action that does not provoke opportunity. They can also choose to stand as a move action, dealing bludgeoning damage equal to their Strength modifier (minimum 1) to a creature within their reach. At 8th level, they deal damage equal to two times their strength modifier with this talent. At 16th level, they deal damage equal to three times their Strength modifier.

Nerve Pinch (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler’s knowledge of anatomy allows them to specifically target their foe’s nerves, lowering their defenses. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or take a -2 penalty to all saving throws for 1 minute. At 10th level, this penalty increases to -3.

Piledriver (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler can lift up a large or smaller creature and drive their head into the ground with tremendous force, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or suffer 1d3 Constitution damage, falling prone regardless of the saving throw. A masked grappler must be 14th level or higher to select this talent.

Pinning Submission (Ex)

A masked grappler increases the damage of submissions to pinned foes by an amount equal to their Constitution modifier. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher and have at least 1 submission talent to select this talent.

Pinning Suplex (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler is capable of both dealing damage and keeping an opponent close, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. Unlike a normal technique, a pinning suplex doesn’t break a grapple, and the masked grappler can attempt a grapple check to pin their foe as a swift action before the end of their round (this has no additional effect against a foe who is already pinned). A masked grappler must be 10th level or higher to select this talent.

Running Dropkick (Ex)

A masked grappler can choose to fly at an opponent without thinking, dealing two times their unarmed strike damage on a charge attack. After this attack, the masked grappler falls prone. At 16th level, this attack deals three times their unarmed strike damage. A masked grappler must be 8th level or higher to select this talent.

Sleeper Hold (Ex)

[submission]: A masked grappler can wrap their arms around a foe’s neck, slowly putting them to sleep. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or become unconscious for 1d3 rounds. Continuing to use this submission does not reset the duration. A masked grappler must be 10th level or higher to select this talent and does not work on foes without heads.

Stiff Clothesline (Ex)

Whenever the masked grappler makes a charge attack using an unarmed strike, if their charge attack is successful, they can make a trip attempt as a swift action (this trip attempt does not provoke an attack of opportunity). If the masked grappler uses the hard whip talent, they can use this talent as an attack of opportunity without needing to make a charge attack.

Stunner (Ex)

[technique]: A masked grappler can strike their opponent with a vicious one two combination, dealing additional damage equal to the masked grappler’s Constitution modifier. The foe must make a Fortitude saving throw or be stunned for 1 round, falling prone regardless of the saving throw. A masked grappler must be 14th level or higher to select this talent.

Team Up (Ex)

When a masked grappler is grappling someone with one or more creatures assisting them, they can add the Strength modifier of one of those other creatures to the damage of a technique. At 10th level, they can add two times that creature’s Strength modifier. A masked grappler must have at least 1 technique talent to select this talent.

Technical Specialist (Ex)

Whenever a masked grappler has a foe pinned, that foe must make two successful grapple checks to end the pin, the first successful grapple check simply bringing them back to being grappled instead of pinned. At 8th level, the foe must make three successful grapple checks, needing to succeed at two to bring them to being grappled instead of pinned. At 16th level, the masked grappler suppresses any freedom of movement spell or effect the target may have.

Tenacious Grappler (Ex)

Whenever a masked grappler uses a technique talent against a foe, they can attempt to grapple that foe as a swift action before their round ends. A masked grappler must be 6th level or higher to select this talent.

This alters vigilante talents.

Signature Move (Ex)

At 5th level, a masked grappler learns how to make one submission or technique their own, adding a special flourish or secret technique to make it all the more devastating. The masked grappler must select 1 submission or technique, designating it as their signature move. Whenever they use their signature move, it deals an additional +1d6 damage and increases any DC associated with it by 1. Whenever a masked grappler gains a new vigilante talent, they can choose to change their signature move. This ability replaces startling appearance.

Chain Grappler (Ex)

At 11th level, whenever the masked wrestler uses a submission or technique, they make two grapple checks, making the second with a -5 penalty. If both grapple checks overcome their foe’s CMD, they deal two times as much damage with that submission or technique. This ability replaces frightening appearance.

Finishing Move (Ex)

At 17th level, a masked grappler has honed their moves to a fine edge, instead imbuing it with much more power. The masked grappler changes their signature move into their finishing move. Whenever the masked grappler uses their finishing move, it deals an additional +3d6 damage and increases any DC associated with it by 2. A masked grappler also designates another submission or technique to be their signature move. This ability replaces stunning appearance.

Master Technician (Ex)

At 20th level, a masked grappler’s moves all have their own flare, everything they do becomes unique to them. All of the masked grappler’s submissions and techniques are treated as signature moves, and they can designate a second submission or technique as a finishing move. This ability replaces vengeance strike.
